topic.title: Introduction
topic.shortdesc: What the dita2epub plugin is, what problem it solves, and what you can expect from it.

body.p: The dita2epub pluginoverviewdita2epub plugin is a transformation for the DITA Open Toolkit that converts DITA content into production-quality EPUB 3 publications. It handles every aspect of the process: structural mapping, metadata extraction, navigation generation, accessibility compliance, font embedding, image optimization, and standards validation.

Unlike minimal proof-of-concept transformations, dita2epub is designed for commercial publishing. It produces output that passes EPUBCheck validation, conforms to WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility guidelines, and renders correctly across major reading systems. The goal is simple: you should be able to take a well-authored DITA bookmap and produce an EPUB that is ready for distribution — to an app store, a corporate intranet, or a reader's bookshelf — without manual post-processing.

section.title: The Problem
section.p: DITA is excellent for structured authoring. Its topic-based architecture, strong typing system, and reuse mechanisms make it the standard for enterprise technical documentation. But DITA was designed for authoring, not for reading. The gap between a well-structured DITA bookmap and a polished digital book is significant:

ul.li: DITA elements must be mapped to their HTML5/XHTML equivalents, respecting EPUB's content model restrictions.
Metadata from the bookmap (title, author, ISBN, copyright, series) must be extracted and expressed in Dublin Core and EPUB-specific OPF properties.
A navigation document must be generated with a table of contents, landmark navigation, and optionally a page list.
Accessibility requirements demand ARIA roles, epub:type attributes, proper heading hierarchy, and alt text validation.
The output must be packaged as a valid ZIP archive with strict ordering requirements (the mimetype file must be first, uncompressed, at byte offset zero).

section.p: The dita2epub plugin handles all of this automatically.

section.title: Key Capabilities
section.p: At a high level, the plugin provides:

ol.li: Complete bookmap support — front matter, chapters, parts, and back matter, with proper DPUB-ARIA role assignment for each section type.

Automatic page generation — cover page, title page, copyright page, table of contents, list of figures, list of tables, consolidated glossary, and back-of-book index, all generated from standard DITA markup.

Rich content transformation — notes with localized labels, tables with column spans and zebra striping, figures with auto-numbering, footnotes with backlinks, code blocks with syntax classes, and blockquotes with attribution.
Professional typography — drop caps, locale-aware quotation marks, CSS hyphenation, and configurable numbering scopes for figures and tables.
Font embedding — with automatic @font-face CSS generation, weight/style detection from filenames, and optional IDPF obfuscation.
Image optimization — JPEG quality adjustment, maximum width scaling, and recursive directory scanning.
Internationalization — twelve languages supported for labels, navigation headings, and note types, with full right-to-left support for Arabic and Hebrew.
Standards compliance — EPUB 3.3, WCAG 2.1 AA, and optional EPUBCheck validation built into the build pipeline.

section.title: A Note on Scope
section.p: This plugin focuses primarily on reflowable EPUB content, which is the best fit for the vast majority of text-centric publications. It also supports fixed layout (FXL) mode for use cases like comics, children's books, and highly designed content where precise visual control is required. The plugin does not support embedded audio, video, or JavaScript interactivity — these are deliberate constraints that keep the output portable across all reading systems.
section.note: The plugin requires DITA-OT 4.4 or later and Java 17 or later. Earlier versions may work but are not tested or supported.
